chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said:
I said, 'What is permissible from Mut'ah?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'As many as you desire.'

key_terms.الْمُتْعَة: Temporary marriage (Mut'ah), a form of marriage with a specified duration and dowry.
key_terms.زُرَارَةُ بْنُ أَعْيَنَ: Zurara ibn A'yan, a prominent companion of the Imams and a major narrator.
key_terms.كَمْ شِئْتَ: As many as you desire, indicating no upper numerical limit.

ai.seo_question: What is the limit on the number of wives in temporary marriage (Mut'ah) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from al-Kafi, Zura'ah ibn A'yan asks the Imam about the limits of Mut'ah, receiving the answer 'as much as you wish,' which Shia jurists interpret as establishing no upper numerical cap on simultaneous temporary marriages. This ruling distinguishes Mut'ah from permanent marriage, where a man is restricted to four wives, and underscores the flexibility of the contract in Shia fiqh. The hadith is often cited to support the view that the only essential conditions for Mut'ah are the specified mahr and duration, without restriction on the number of partners.
